tasks.title: Build literature and benchmark novelty matrix
definition_of_done: Primary-source literature matrix covers medical multimodal, dynamic/sparse computation, graph faithfulness and Clinical Front Door work

evidence: Partial 2026-08-26: 18 external references verified against primary sources (Crossref REST, DOI CSL-JSON, PubMed E-utilities, arXiv API, JMLR BibTeX) and formatted in APA 7 in docs/academic/PROJECT_IDEA.md. No reference was written from memory. Still owed for this task: the novelty comparison matrix, the search protocol, and the baseline shortlist required by the definition of done

Revised 2026-08-26 on the project owner's instruction to drop pre-2020 sources: the reference set is now 19 entries spanning 2020-2026, weighted toward current multimodal medical models (Med-PaLM M, Med-Gemini, LLaVA-Med, BiomedCLIP) and contemporary evidence on deployment failure, leakage, and explanation faithfulness. MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, BraTS and VQA-RAD were removed from the document but remain on the TASK-0005 dataset feasibility list; the cited candidates are MIMIC-IV, SLAKE and CT-RATE

Narrowed 2026-08-26 to 8 references on the owner's instruction, rebalanced so that 5 of 8 are AI/ML architecture or method papers (Han 2022 dynamic networks, Jiang 2024 Mixtral, Li 2023 LLaVA-Med, Turpin 2023 CoT faithfulness, Hamamci 2026 3D CT foundation model). Each reference now supports a distinct claim with no redundancy. Deliberately not cited: any base-model family paper, because the project has not decided what it builds on and citing one would pre-empt that decision

Range tightened 2026-08-26 to 2022-2026 on the owner's instruction. Wong et al. (2021) was the only entry outside it and was replaced by Bedi et al. (2025) JAMA, whose systematic review of 519 health care LLM evaluations reports that 5% used real patient care data, 95.4% measured only accuracy, and 1.2% measured calibration and uncertainty. Those figures were read from the PubMed abstract, not recalled, and they now carry the document's novelty argument

Extended 2026-08-26 to 13 references (all 2022-2026) by closing four gaps the document claimed but did not support: multimodal biomedical AI as a field (Acosta 2022), EHR and longitudinal foundation models (Wornow 2023), per-patient predictive uncertainty (Banerji 2023), and human-AI collaboration (Goh 2024 RCT), plus the DECIDE-AI reporting guideline for early-stage clinical decision-support evaluation (Vasey 2022). Reported figures from Bedi and Goh were read from PubMed abstracts, not recalled
